digest.component_or_area: Terraform state management and SSM parameter handling
propositions: Operator-seeded SSM SecureString secrets with value='CHANGEME' plus lifecycle.ignore_changes=[value] persist plaintext values in remote terraform state (S3 rebar-tfstate-896586841071) despite ignore_changes suppressing diffs, because the AWS provider reads live values into state on every refresh/import.

Twenty-three secrets in cleartext are readable by any S3 GetObject-permitted principal (currently account administrators only, not the EC2 instance role), collapsing the SecureString access tier to state-bucket ACL.
Terraform state versioning (149 retained versions with no expiry) preserves all historical secret values in cleartext indefinitely, making exposure window unbounded in time.

Remediation migrates three resources to terraform write-only arguments value_wo + value_wo_version (never persisted to state by provider design), requires terraform >= 1.11 and AWS provider ~> 5.79, and necessitates deferred operator task to re-seed/rotate secrets and scrub historical state versions.
Lockstep updates required in opcert-plan-assertions.sh, test_opcert_deploy_infra.py, and documentation to assert value_wo invariant and reflect new secret handling contract.
New hermetic guard check_ssm_secret_state.py (wired to make lint) prevents regression by flagging any SecureString with literal value or ignore_changes=[value] outside the generated-value case.
